Set and Reset signals can be either synchronous or asynchronous, depending on the design requirements. They may also be referred to as latches or flip-flops, which are commonly used in computer science and digital electronics for storing state information.

Set and Reset signals are characterized by their recovery and removal times, which ensure the input signals remain within specified limits long enough for the flip-flop to change state or maintain its current state. Recovery time guarantees sufficient holding of input signals before the rising edge of the clock, while removal time ensures proper operation after the clock event.
